summary:
I'm a Melbourne-based front-end engineer with nine years shipping production web interfaces across banking, commerce, and client-facing platforms. My stack centers on React and TypeScript with SCSS, Webpack, and Gulp, backed by REST, SOAP, and GraphQL integrations—the same API-first model agencies rely on when building on headless CMS and DXP platforms. I'm targeting the Lead Front End Developer role at Core dna because I want depth in product UX on a platform digital teams actually build on, not one-off consulting delivery.

At CMB I built accessible React SPAs with Redux, HTML5/CSS3, and Bootstrap, including Global Wire Payments (GPOW) workflows with disciplined TDD and strong unit-test coverage in a regulated banking context. On Holland America and Seabourn cruise platforms I delivered bookings, itineraries, live location, payment, and onboard modules—commerce-adjacent UX driven by Express APIs. Earlier Upwork delivery included payment and banking UI modules with Agile sprints in JIRA; across freelance work I've owned architecture, code review, and cross-training peers on UI patterns.

I'm based in Melbourne and aligned with Prahran hybrid work. Core dna 2.0's focus on showcase platform features and partner community fits how I already work: translating complex API backends into reliable, accessible front-end solutions for external users and agency customers. I'm ready to bring that lead scope—mentoring, technical ownership, and customer-facing delivery—to your DXP engineering team.
coverLetter:
Hello Core dna team,

Core dna 2.0’s push to unify content, commerce, and collaboration in one DXP is exactly the kind of platform UX challenge I want to lead. You build the stack agencies and digital teams ship on — I have spent the last several years shipping accessible React front ends on top of REST, SOAP, and GraphQL services, and I want that work to sit on a product other teams build with, not just one-off client sites.

Over nine years of front-end delivery, I have owned complex UI modules in regulated and high-traffic settings. At CMB, I built React/Redux SPAs for banking operators and customers — HTML5, SCSS, Bootstrap — with NVDA and JAWS testing baked into delivery. I led the Global Wire Payments (GPOW) interface for Wells Fargo with strong TDD discipline and high unit-test coverage on wire, bank-to-bank, and group payment flows. That combination — platform-scale React, accessibility standards, and test-driven quality — maps directly to showcasing Core dna’s front end to your partner community.

Before that, on Holland America and Seabourn cruise platforms, I delivered bookings, itineraries, live location, payments, and onboard deck booking features — commerce-adjacent UX powered by Express REST APIs. On client engagements I have also shipped payment and enrolment modules with Agile sprints, JIRA, Webpack, and Gulp pipelines. I have cross-trained peers through code review and pattern documentation; I am ready to formalize that as Lead FE mentorship on your team.

I have not shipped on a headless CMS vendor stack yet, but API-first React integration is my daily pattern — the same model your DXP exposes to agencies. I am Melbourne-based, comfortable with Prahran on-site or hybrid, and available to start when you need. I would welcome a conversation about how you are approaching lead front-end ownership on Core dna 2.0.
